t:
Not later than January 15, I960, the President shall make a report to the Congress setting forth a plan, to be carried out over a period of ten years (June 30, 1968, to June 30, 1978), for the elimination of all substandard housing and the realization of the goal referred to in section 1601. Such plan shall—

    (1) 
indicate the number of new or rehabilitated housing units which it is anticipated will have to be provided, with or without Government assistance, during each fiscal year of the ten-year period, in order to achieve the objectives of the plan, showing the number of such units which it is anticipated will have to be provided under each of the various Federal programs designed to assist in the provision of housing;
 
    (2) 
indicate the reduction in the number of occupied substandard housing units which it is anticipated will have to occur during each fiscal year of the ten-year period in order to achieve the objectives of the plan;
 
    (3) 
provide an estimate of the cost of carrying out the plan for each of the various Federal programs and for each fiscal year during the ten-year period to the extent that such costs will be reflected in the Federal budget;
 
    (4) 
make recommendations with respect to the legislative and administrative actions necessary or desirable to achieve the objectives of the plan; and
 
    (5) 
provide such other pertinent data estimates, and recommendations as the President deems advisable.

fable.w: The section only requires the President to report a ten-year housing plan to Congress, and both actors are inside the federal government. The tempting reading is that a formal plan with recommendations on legislative and administrative action implies consultation, but the text requires no consultation with states, the public, experts, or any other outside party. It also contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the President shall make a report to the Congress setting forth a plan

qwen_block.w: The section requires the President to submit a report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve consultation or coordination with outside parties. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or the public.
qwen_block.s: Not later than January 15, I960, the President shall make a report to the Congress setting forth a plan

opus.w: This section only requires the President to send Congress a report containing a housing plan, estimates and recommendations. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. The section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue for states, localities, experts or the public. The phrase "with or without Government assistance" describes how housing units might be built, not anyone outside the government taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: the President shall make a report to the Congress setting forth a plan, to be carried out over a period of ten years
opus.b: The tempting reading is that a ten-year national housing plan with "recommendations with respect to the legislative and administrative actions" must involve outside input. That reading fails: the only actors here are the President, who writes the report, and Congress, which receives it. Both are inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the President to submit a report to Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, and reports to Congress or its committees are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. There is no mention of consulting with or coordinating with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities) before making the decision or creating the plan.
qwen_chat.s: Not later than January 15, I960, the President shall make a report to the Congress setting forth a plan...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the President is making a report to Congress, this involves "participation" in a broad sense of government interaction. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. Furthermore, the section does not mention any consultation with states, local governments, the public, or other outside entities.
